newsitem.title: CHINA: China-no goal for yuan convertibility on cap/acct.
newsitem.headline: China-no goal for yuan convertibility on cap/acct.

text.p: China has no timetable for making its currency convertible on the capital account, the official Xinhua news agency said on Friday.

"As for when we can make the yuan convertible under the capital account or even freely convertible, we have not worked out a specific timetable," Xinhua quoted a spokesman of the State Administration of Exchange Control, as saying.
Central bank governor Dai Xianglong told Reuters in a recent interview that China still needed a "fairly long period" before making its currency convertible on the capital account.
"Making the renminbi yuan freely convertible under both the current and capital accounts is a long-term goal of China's reform in its foreign exchange system," the spokesman said.
Xinhua on Thursday quoted Dai as saying China would make the yuan convertible under the current account as of December 1.

China would retain some restrictions on transactions under the capital account, including those on direct investment, international loans and securities trading, after the current account became convertible, the spokesman said.
China has been gradually dismantling curbs on the currency's conversion, removing in July restrictions on current account sales of foreign exchange to foreign firms.
Chinese individuals currently cannot buy or sell foreign exchange freely nor make payments in foreign exchange freely.
